title: Field transitions for integral-normalized finite scalar comparisons
statement: Fix the finite-field, scheme, compactification, native geometry, supplied Realizations and supplied exceptional coefficient System S of the parent, with l invertible in all residue fields of X. Fix canonical completed-to-native changes agreeing with every integral coefficient presentation. Suppose a family alpha E of finite rational natural isomorphisms is supplied, between inclusion E followed by S.closed and target.J, and inclusion E followed by source.J and actual c. Assume that on every integral representative its component equals the explicitly constructed systemIntegralMap. Then alpha commutes with each actual common-stage isoToStage: F.map t followed by alpha E at A.toStage equals alpha at A.stage on A.obj followed by H.map t. This asserts only field-transition compatibility for supplied integral-normalized finite comparisons; it constructs no isomorphism and performs no common-stage descent.

source.place: Final exceptional-adjunction sentence; ordinary comparison, closure transport and scalar realization.

proof.text: Represent the rational input by its unchanged underlying integral object. Use residue Tor to regard it as finite-Tor. Apply faithful derived sections and the supplied integral component formulas to identify both alpha components with the explicitly constructed scalar maps. Expand their two boundary comparisons. The commonComparison cocycle, source and target common_field equations, rational_normalized and integralLeft_normalized reduce the transition equation to the same integral scalar square.

proof.text: Use coefficient_scalar and the normalized completed tensor comparison to identify successive scalar extensions with their direct composite. comparison_composition identifies the two proper/open scalar mates under the balanced tensor associators; proper counit triangle identities and the open tensor-unit normalization identify the chosen maps. Cancel the inverse realization boundaries and reflect equality through faithful sections. The integral component formulas transfer this equality to alpha. The identity inclusion inserts the same tensor unit, and zero inputs and empty schemes use the same equations.
